accepted_source_uncertainties.review: The opening إلا and أمر fragment has incomplete linkage at this page boundary. Both notes accurately limit the uncertainty to that linkage; neither supplies a missing antecedent or condition.
مثاله carries an unidentified masculine possessive in this excerpt. EN 'its' and ID '-nya' are retained with explicit uncertainty, not resolved into a particular drawing or victim.
The continuous source does not explicitly delimit every invocation, quotation fragment and commentary. Both global boundary notes are justified and do not license canonical completion.
Unvocalized يمنع supports active prevent and passive be prevented/withheld. Both notes retain negation and qualify actor/linkage instead of presenting either voice as certain.
The referent of له before no beginning/no interruption is not secure in the broken sequence. Both possessive-referent notes are warranted; both negatives remain translated.

The inheritance-root verb and the construction لا يورثك في غيرك غيرك are difficult as printed. Both literal provisional renderings preserve the repeated other-than-You terms and explicitly qualify reading and meaning; no fluent doctrinal repair is asserted.

Quotation extent around the blaze/scalp/flame sequence is not marked in the source. Both notes qualify extent while translating the printed negative flame clause; neither claims an authenticated canonical quotation boundary.

محسناً is correctly retained as muḥsinan with a doing-good semantic qualification. Its construction here is awkward; both notes flag role without changing it into a settled object, addressee or reward clause.
بكذا is an unusual complement of the descent request as printed. Both preserve with/dengan and qualify its relation to the descent rather than silently replacing ب with upon/على.
Printed حادر is not the familiar حاذر. Both retain ḥādir and flag reading/meaning; neither invents a cautious-person gloss from a silently substituted consonant.

تزهو في حقك has an uncertain actor/connection in its relative construction. Glories/bermegah is a defensible lexical qualification of تزهو; both notes also preserve the with-respect-to-You phrase and do not assert a repaired subject.

The action and linkage of ويحول are opaque in the printed sequence. Both retain yaḥūl with an explicitly local reading/meaning note, while still translating malakūt, deferred, determinations, decrees, sanctities and the none-but-You restriction.

Both مدبر and التدبير are masculine, making attachment of الأزلي الجليل المتعالي insufficiently explicit in the undelimited chain. Both notes preserve all three attributes and order without claiming a single syntactic attachment.

الأهلي is printed, not الإلهي. Its intended sense in this permission formula is unclear; both notes properly retain al-ahlī rather than inventing divine permission. The uncertainty concerns intended sense, not a claim that the lexical form itself is absent.

The unvocalized compelling/world clause has uncertain actor and syntactic connection. Both qualified renderings retain the world, until-link, and some/part subduing some/part, not a new agent or total annihilation.

مصادمتي contains the petitioner's first-person possessive but no explicit counterpart. Both notes correctly qualify who confronts whom, while keeping his senses and his spirituality distinct from my clash and my presence.

Printed أجعل can be read as first-person I make; an intended imperative would normally have a different initial orthography. Both notes explicitly distinguish printed person from intended make!, preserving the uncertainty rather than normalizing the text.

The unvocalized جعلتها ending permits first-/second-person readings in this context. Both notes qualify the provisional I/aku arranging statement; neither presents first-person authorship as established. The differing mnemonic itself remains unchanged.

The referent of masculine singular إليه is not explicit. Both targets preserve attributed-to-it/kepadanya with a referent note and do not silently change the source suffix into an asserted plural relation.
